set.body: The sidebar grouped concepts by their first path segment only, so a bundle with agents/foo/bar.md collapsed every nested file under a single 'agents' heading. Build a real nested directory tree from concept paths and render it as a collapsible tree, with search filtering that keeps parent directories of any match.
set.title: Nested collapsible file tree in the sidebar

set.body: Opening a real repository pulled build output into the bundle: the three filesystem walkers (Rust desktop, Node dev-server, browser upload) each had their own idea of what to skip, and only skipped dotfiles. Browser folder upload additionally flattened nested paths because it stripped a leading path segment from every file rather than just the picker's root folder.
set.title: Filesystem walkers pull in build output and flatten upload paths

set.body: The repo was exported from a Grok sandbox with no work tracking, no CI, and an AGENTS.md that was Grok sandbox boilerplate rather than project documentation. Install the worklog toolchain (CLI, git hooks, CI workflow, config pointing at GitHub Issues and the GitHub wiki) and write a real CLAUDE.md covering the dual web/desktop architecture, the filesystem-jail mirror invariant, and the dead code a newcomer will otherwise trust.
set.title: Scaffold worklog and write the project agent guide

set.body: eslint reports errors that CI will never see: the ignore list omits src-tauri/target, so on any machine that has run cargo build, eslint lints generated Tauri build scripts. A fresh CI checkout has no target directory, so the gate would pass green while every developer's local run fails. Three source files also carry trivial prefer-const violations that block turning lint into a gate at all.
set.title: Lint gate is unlandable: ignore holes plus prefer-const errors

set.body: CI runs only the worklog ledger invariants, so a type error, a lint failure, a broken build, or a failing test merges to main unopposed. Add a workflow that runs typecheck, lint, both JS test tiers, the web build, the browser end-to-end suite, and the Rust tests, then require those checks before anything can merge.
set.title: Application quality gate on every pull request

set.body: Nothing verifies that the app shell actually lays out correctly. A previous regression collapsed the sidebar and main panel into the same 280px column and was caught only by eye; the fix is documented in a code comment with no test behind it. Add the minimum instrumentation to make layout assertable, a design spec with a wireframe and a pass/fail rubric for the Editor view, and a structural test suite that enforces the rubric rows a machine can judge.
set.title: UI spec, wireframe and layout rubric for the Editor view

set.body: Three end-to-end tests failed on main and had presumably never passed: the repository was exported from a sandbox where the browser suite was not run in this configuration. The web build is server-rendered, so the static copy the tests waited on was visible before React hydrated. Each test then clicked a real, enabled button whose event handler was not yet attached, and failed with a symptom (dialog never appeared) that pointed nowhere near the cause. Tests must wait for a signal that only exists after client-side initialisation.
set.title: End-to-end tests interact with the app before it hydrates

set.body: Several desktop projects are developed side by side on one machine, often by different agents at once, and every Vite template ships the same hardcoded dev-server port. When two collide the failure is quiet rather than loud: the browser test runner reuses whatever is already listening, so the entire end-to-end suite runs against a different project's application and fails with assertions that look like bugs in this one. The port must be probed for availability, remembered between runs, and read from one place by every consumer.
set.title: Dev server port collides with other projects on the same machine

set.body: The repository ships a Prettier config but was never formatted with it: around 29 source files fail a check at any print width. The sweep was deliberately deferred while two pull requests were open because it would have conflicted with them. With the board clear it can land as one atomic reformat, after which a format check costs nothing to enforce.

set.body: The desktop storage provider has no automated coverage in any tier. The frontend sends a command name and argument shape to the Rust backend; rename either side and nothing fails anywhere, because the browser tests never touch that path and the Rust tests never touch the frontend. Add a component-level test runner with a mocked interprocess bridge and pin that contract.
set.title: Desktop storage provider has no JavaScript test coverage

set.body: Verifying the desktop application means launching it and looking at it by hand. Add opt-in automation surfaces behind a build feature so a machine can drive the real window: a bridge for agent-driven inspection during development, and a WebDriver server for scripted regression runs. Both must be absent from release builds, not merely disabled.
set.title: Desktop app cannot be driven by automation
